questions.name: anomaly_probe
questions.instructions: Does this session skeleton show ANY non-trivial operational friction, user correction/pushback, violated assumption, silent failure, environment/OS/shell surprise, workflow/CI/git pitfall, or explicit durable rule/lesson?

questions.name: user_correction_probe
questions.instructions: Did the human user explicitly correct a mistake, reject an assumption/behavior, state a standing preference/policy, or ask to codify/distill a workflow rule?

questions.name: primary_axis
questions.instructions: Classify the highest-signal operational lesson or friction in this session skeleton.

choices.description: Routine coding, Q&A, or exploration with clean progress and no reusable operational friction.
Ordinary repo-local syntax, type, test, or business-logic bug fixed locally with no cross-repo lesson.
PR merge gating, CI runner/check behavior, branch/worktree cleanup, git identity, or release verification.
Cross-OS differences, non-interactive shell PATH, hooks, console window flash, sandbox/junction/filesystem isolation, or CLI binary drift.
Subagent/worker delegation, acceptance verification, skill authoring/installation, memory behavior, or operating contracts.
Dotfiles/template source-vs-target drift, cross-device bootstrap, or repository boundary/ownership rules.
ESCAPE HATCH: Real operational friction, hidden failure mode, or reusable engineering lesson that does NOT fit the specific categories above.

questions.name: durability
questions.instructions: Rate whether this session likely contains a durable lesson worth auditing for cross-repo playbooks, reusable skills/evals, or device/hook configuration rather than single-app feature work.

levels.label: none
levels.description: Pure single-app feature/bug work or empty/trivial session.

levels.label: repo_local
levels.description: Useful within one specific tool/repo, moderate reuse.

levels.label: cross_repo_systemic
levels.description: High-leverage cross-repo, cross-OS, or agent-harness rule/guardrail.

questions.name: anomaly_probe
questions.instructions: Did an operational surprise, workflow/tooling pitfall, silent failure, environment mismatch, or user workflow/policy correction occur in this span?

questions.name: mechanism_v1
questions.instructions: Classify the underlying mechanism of this span.

choices.description: Clean progress, UI/business-logic tweak, or ordinary repo-local code/type/test/CLI-typo fix.
PR merge gating, CI checks/billing/runners, branch/worktree safety, git identity, or release verification.
Cross-OS differences, non-interactive shell PATH/hooks, console window spawn, filesystem/sandbox/junction isolation, or binary/config root mismatch.
Subagent delegation/acceptance, skill authoring/naming/installers, memory behavior, or agent operating rules.
Template source-vs-generated target drift, cross-device onboarding, or repo boundary/ownership.
ESCAPE HATCH: A genuine operational failure mode or reusable engineering rule that does NOT fit the specific buckets above.

questions.name: reusable_guardrail
questions.instructions: Rate whether this span reveals a reusable engineering guardrail/rule across repositories, skills, or device configuration versus single-project work.

levels.label: ephemeral_or_app_local
levels.description: No lesson, transient glitch, or single-app code/UI/domain detail.

levels.label: candidate_pattern
levels.description: Plausible tooling/workflow friction worth inspecting with surrounding context.

levels.label: high_value_guardrail
levels.description: Clear, reusable operational guardrail, silent-harm trap, or explicit standing workflow rule.

questions.name: anomaly_probe
questions.instructions: Does this span contain concrete evidence of an operational pitfall, silent failure mode, or explicit human workflow/policy directive (excluding slash commands, routine status notifications, and single-app feature work)?

questions.name: evidence_backing
questions.instructions: Verify whether this span contains CONCRETE EVIDENCE of an operational lesson/rule (directly observed tool/hook/CI/env failure + diagnosis, OR an explicit human workflow/policy directive), versus routine progress or boilerplate.

choices.description: Slash commands (/clear, /plugin), task-notification plumbing, routine green checks, or unverified speculation without a concrete pitfall or user directive.
Concrete bug/requirement, but strictly specific to one app's UI, CSS, domain math, cloud deployment config, or local syntax/type error.
Directly evidenced cross-session operational trap, silent failure mode, or explicit human workflow/governance rule.

questions.name: taxonomy_v2
questions.instructions: Classify into the refined operational taxonomy. Choose routine_or_app_local whenever the span is slash-command noise, single-app feature/bug work, or pure task-notification status.

choices.description: Routine coding/tests, slash commands (/clear, /plugin), background task notifications, local syntax/type/CLI-flag fixes, or single-app domain/UI/deploy details.
PR merge gates, auto-merge races, CI runner/billing blocks, branch/worktree cleanup safety, or git identity routing.
Cross-OS differences, non-interactive shell PATH/hooks, console window spawning (CREATE_NO_WINDOW vs DETACHED_PROCESS), sandbox/junction/HOME isolation, or CLI version/config-root drift.
Preserving concurrent user/agent uncommitted edits during staging/commits, or stripping ANSI color/TTY escape codes when scraping CLI output.
Subagent/worker delegation & independent verification, skill naming/packaging/installers, or agent memory / consolidation behavior.
Dotfiles/template source-vs-target drift, run_once partial-failure wedging, or cross-repo canonical ownership boundaries.
ESCAPE HATCH: A proven, cross-repo reusable engineering guardrail that genuinely does not fit any category above.

questions.name: systemic_score
questions.instructions: Score cross-repository operational leverage. Penalize single-app fixes, transient network blips, and mid-flight status updates to 0.

levels.label: discard
levels.description: Noise, boilerplate, transient error, or single-app detail.

levels.label: high_leverage_rule
levels.description: High-impact cross-repo guardrail preventing silent data loss, premature merge, config clobbering, or recurring multi-OS friction.

questions.name: novelty_status
questions.instructions: Compare the operational lesson in the SPAN against the CURRENT CODIFIED BASELINE prepended above. Classify whether it is already covered, an uncovered target gap, owned by a sibling repository, or local noise.

choices.description: The core rule or fix in this span is ALREADY explicitly covered by the baseline documents, scripts, or tests.
A concrete cross-repo playbook, onboarding diagnostic, or harness check gap that belongs in the target repository and is NOT yet covered in the baseline.
Real reusable operational trap/lesson, but canonical ownership belongs to a sibling skill or dotfiles repository rather than the target repository.
Upon closer inspection against the baseline, this span is single-project implementation work, mid-flight status, or lacks a durable rule.

questions.name: actionability
questions.instructions: Rate how directly actionable and high-leverage this span is for a NEW improvement to the target repository today.

levels.label: none
levels.description: Already covered, owned by another repo, or local noise.

levels.label: supporting_evidence
levels.description: Useful recurrence evidence for a cross-repo pattern or routing boundary.

levels.label: direct_gap
levels.description: Directly proves an uncovered failure mode that target docs or harness checks should guard against.

[L10 USER] Enable auto-merge so it merges once CI passes.
[L14 TOOL_OK Bash(gh pr merge 123 --auto --squash)] Merged immediately at 13:10:42Z before GitHub Actions check runs even registered (13:10:43Z), because main branch had no enforced status check protection rules.

SPAN anchor:pos_3
[L12 HOOK_ERROR] /bin/sh: 1: node: not found in stop-review-gate-hook.mjs
[L18 ASST] `which node` works in interactive zsh because `.zshrc` loads fnm/mise, but hooks run under non-interactive `/bin/sh` where shims are absent from PATH.

SPAN anchor:pos_4
[L20 USER] Every time the background check runs on Windows, black cmd windows flash on my screen and steal focus. Never let subprocesses pop console windows.
[L25 ASST] Python `subprocess.run` on Windows spawns a console window when invoked from a GUI/daemon host unless `creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW` is passed.
